numerical_failure.observed_behavior: special.gammainc(np.nan, arg) returns finite values (e.g. 0. and 1.) for some infinite or finite arguments with NaN input: printed [nan nan 0. nan 1. nan] for arg=[-inf,-1,0,1,inf,nan]; special.gammainc(arg, np.nan) returns 0. at arg=inf: [nan nan nan nan 0. nan]. Related: special.chdtrc(-1, -1) returns 1.0 instead of NaN, and special.chdtrc(np.nan, arg) returns [1. 1. nan nan nan nan] with finite values for -inf and -1.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Any NaN argument to gammainc or gammaincc should propagate NaN, so results should be nan for every element where either a or x is nan; chdtrc with a NaN degrees-of-freedom argument should return NaN, and chdtrc with negative x should return NaN (domain error) rather than 1.0.
trigger_conditions: NaN passed as the a (shape) argument of gammainc or gammaincc with finite or infinite x
NaN passed as the x argument of gammainc or gammaincc with infinite a-values giving finite results
chdtrc called with negative x (e.g. -1) and/or NaN degrees of freedom returns 1.0 instead of NaN
oracle_clues: Issue text states the expected behaviour: NaN input should yield NaN results, consistent with chdtr returning nan for negative degrees of freedom
Maintainer comment: to be consistent, chdtrc should return NaN here
Fix adds explicit isnan checks in igam and igamc returning quiet NaN; chdtrc fix sets SF_ERROR_DOMAIN and returns NaN for x<0
Tests added for nan arguments to gammainc(c) and chdtr(c)

category_specific_evidence: Special values involved are NaN (as the a or x argument of gammainc/gammaincc) and, in the test inputs, +/-inf and -0.0; the stated handling is NaN propagation: if either a or x is NaN, return quiet NaN before the x<0 or a<0 domain check (igam.h diff, igamc diff).

Issue #21317: special.gammainc(np.nan, [-inf, -1., 0., 1., inf, nan]) printed [nan nan 0. nan 1. nan] and special.gammainc([-inf, -1., 0., 1., inf, nan], np.nan) printed [nan nan nan nan 0. nan]; the expected output is all nan.

Issue #20972 and PR discussion: chdtrc(-1, -1) returns 1.0 instead of NaN; chdtrc(np.nan, [-inf, -1., 0., 1., inf, nan]) returns [1. 1. nan nan nan nan] where the expected output is all nan; the reviewer says chdtrc should return NaN for these inputs to be consistent with chdtr.
The chdtrc fix sets SF_ERROR_DOMAIN and returns NaN for x<0 (per oracle clues and commit message 'fix chdtrc out of domain case').
test_gammainc.py adds test_a_nan and test_x_nan, asserting np.isnan(sc.gammainc(np.nan, x)) and np.isnan(sc.gammainc(a, np.nan)) for a or x in [-inf, -1.0, -0.0, 0.0, inf, nan].
